Event type: RBI repo-rate decision and surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Funding costs, credit and valuation discount rates
Required guardrail: Compare decision with pre-release consensus; rate cut is not automatically bullish
LLM guidance: RBI repo-rate decision. Judge against consensus if the text gives it: a surprise cut or a larger-than-expected cut = +1; a hike or hawkish surprise = -1; a decision in line with expectations = 0 (already priced in). A cut is NOT automatically bullish. Mark provenance official/reported ONLY if the text states the decision with specifics (MPC vote, official statement, the new rate); a social post or clickbait claim of a hike or cut without them is 'unverified'. 'RBI may hike by 2027' is an expectation, not a decision.

Event type: RBI stance, forecasts and guidance
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Expected future policy path
Required guardrail: Separate current decision from future guidance
LLM guidance: RBI stance, forecasts, guidance, MPC minutes. More dovish than expected = +1; more hawkish = -1; unchanged or as expected = 0 (priced in). Forecasts of what the RBI might do are expectations, not guidance; a post without the official wording is unverified.

Event type: RBI liquidity operations and reserve requirements
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Banking-system liquidity and funding stress
Required guardrail: Quantify net liquidity effect and implementation dates

Event type: Fed rate decision and forward guidance
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Global yields, dollar and EM risk appetite
Required guardrail: A dovish cut can be offset by recession information
LLM guidance: Fed decision, minutes or forward guidance. A decision in line with expectations is priced in (0). A hawkish or dovish surprise vs expectations moves it. Previews and prediction-market odds for a FUTURE meeting are expectations, not decisions.

Event type: Fed balance-sheet or liquidity programme
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Global funding conditions
Required guardrail: Record change versus existing programme, not repeated descriptions

Event type: PBoC stimulus and reserve-rate changes
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: China demand and regional risk appetite
Required guardrail: Identify whether announcement is new and implementable

Event type: BoJ policy and yen-funding shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Carry-trade unwinds and global liquidity
Required guardrail: Track yen and global-risk confirmation separately

Event type: ECB or other major central-bank surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Global rates and cross-border capital allocation
Required guardrail: Promote only material deviations from expectations

Event type: India CPI and food-inflation surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: RBI expectations and household purchasing power
Required guardrail: Capture actual, consensus, previous and revisions

Event type: India GDP or GVA surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Earnings and policy expectations
Required guardrail: Preserve initial-release vintage and base effects
LLM guidance: India GDP/GVA print or revision. Score only if the text reports a GDP/GVA figure or revision. Higher growth than expected or than the previous period = +1, lower = -1 (use the forecast or previous figure if the text gives one). Commentary, quotes or outlook about growth ('CEO says growth is strong') is not a print: relates=false.

Event type: India PMI, IIP or core-industry surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Industrial and service-sector demand
Required guardrail: Do not combine unlike indicators into one raw surprise
LLM guidance: India PMI, IIP or core-industry print. Direction from the actual vs forecast or previous reading: accelerating expansion = +1, slowing or contraction = -1. A forecast or opinion piece is not a print: relates=false.

Event type: India WPI, trade balance or external-account shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Imported costs, rupee and external financing
Required guardrail: Separate original figures from later revisions

Event type: Material India growth-forecast revision
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Earnings expectations and country risk
Required guardrail: Forecast change is opinion, not realised economic data

Event type: US CPI, core CPI or PPI surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Fed expectations, yields and dollar
Required guardrail: Record economic-growth regime and forecast surprise

Event type: US PCE or core PCE inflation surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Fed policy expectations
Required guardrail: Distinguish monthly from annual rates

Event type: US payrolls, unemployment or wage surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Rates and US end-demand
Required guardrail: Strong jobs can be positive growth news and negative rates news
LLM guidance: US payrolls, unemployment or wage print. For India the net effect usually runs through yields and the dollar: a hot jobs/wage print that raises rate-hike expectations or lifts yields and the dollar = -1; a soft print that raises rate-cut expectations without recession fear = +1. If the text gives no consensus or market reaction, direction 0 with low confidence.

Event type: US GDP, PMI, retail-sales or consumer-demand shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Export demand and recession/rates repricing
Required guardrail: Use proper release authority for each indicator; do not infer it from these examples alone
LLM guidance: US GDP, PMI, retail sales or consumer-demand data. Weak data that raises recession fear = -1; moderately soft data is +1 only if the text says it raises rate-cut hopes; strong data is usually 0 or -1 via yields. If unclear, direction 0.

Event type: China or Europe activity and inflation surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Metals demand and global growth
Required guardrail: China stimulus is a separate policy event
LLM guidance: China or Europe activity and inflation print. Stronger-than-expected activity = +1 (metals, global demand); weaker = -1. Use the forecast or previous figure if given; otherwise low confidence.

Event type: Tariff hike, threat, effective date or exemption
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Export margins, global growth and risk premium
Required guardrail: Track proposed, signed, effective, stayed and repealed as different states

Event type: Tariff pause, truce or trade-agreement progress
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Trade uncertainty and exporter competitiveness
Required guardrail: Negotiation optimism is weaker evidence than a signed enforceable change

Event type: Russian-oil, energy or financial sanctions
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: India oil sourcing, trade and financing
Required guardrail: Identify which goods, entities and countries are actually covered

Event type: Technology export restrictions or critical-input controls
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Technology demand and industrial supply chains
Required guardrail: Confirm legal scope and implementation

Event type: US visa, immigration or outsourcing rule change
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Indian IT staffing costs and delivery model
Required guardrail: Add relevant official immigration agency notices before production

Event type: India-Pakistan military or diplomatic escalation
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Country risk, travel/trade disruption and risk appetite
Required guardrail: Attribute claims to each party; distinguish report from confirmation

Event type: Middle East war or infrastructure attack
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Oil/LNG supply and global risk
Required guardrail: Link oil response to the same root event to prevent double counting

Event type: Ceasefire, peace talks or military de-escalation
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Removal of geopolitical risk premium
Required guardrail: Claim, agreement and verified implementation are different stages

Event type: Shipping-route closure, blockade or insurance disruption
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Energy availability and imported freight costs
Required guardrail: Route must be materially relevant to India or world supply

Event type: US or major-country election/political shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Future policy uncertainty and regional risk appetite
Required guardrail: Do not infer victory from incomplete counting without attribution
LLM guidance: US or major-country election or political shock. An outcome that raises policy uncertainty or tariff risk = -1; a clear market-friendly outcome = +1. Pre-election speculation or polls = 0 unless the text states a market effect.

Event type: US fiscal shutdown or debt-ceiling disruption
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Data availability, sovereign risk and global liquidity
Required guardrail: Ordinary political debate needs a materiality threshold

Event type: Indian general/state election or coalition shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Policy continuity and spending expectations
Required guardrail: Separate exit polls from official results

Event type: Material domestic security attack or disruption
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Country risk, travel and activity disruption
Required guardrail: Require reliable confirmation; preserve exact first-seen timestamp

Event type: OPEC+ production decision or surprise compliance change
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Crude supply, India import bill and inflation
Required guardrail: Differentiate announced quota from realised output

Event type: Oil/LNG supply outage or reserve release
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Imported energy costs and supply security
Required guardrail: Do not count the same war shock a second time at full weight

Event type: Petroleum inventories or demand-outlook surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Oil price and global-demand expectations
Required guardrail: Include consensus for inventory releases and relevance threshold

Event type: Major industrial-metal or commodity supply restriction
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Input margins and metal-producer demand
Required guardrail: Company/sector signs can oppose the index-wide effect

Event type: Union Budget tax, capex or fiscal-deficit surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Demand, public investment and funding costs
Required guardrail: Preopen model must not consume same-day speech after its cutoff
LLM guidance: Union Budget tax, capex and fiscal-deficit surprise relative to expectations. Tax relief, higher capex, credible consolidation = +1; tax hikes on markets (STT, capital gains) or fiscal slippage = -1. Budget previews and wishlists are not events.

Event type: GST or material direct/indirect tax change
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Consumption and corporate margins
Required guardrail: Track proposal versus final notification and effective date

Event type: STT, derivatives or market-structure rule change
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Trading costs, participation and market liquidity
Required guardrail: Scheduled expiry alone belongs in context, not as a surprise event

Event type: Bank/NBFC lending, provisioning or project-finance rule
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Credit supply and financial-sector earnings
Required guardrail: Separate regulation from a monetary-policy rate decision

Event type: RBI FX, hedging or exposure-limit rule
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Rupee liquidity, bank earnings and FX risk
Required guardrail: Track rule scope, transition period and exposure concentration

Event type: Government sector support, subsidy or procurement change
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Sector demand and earnings
Required guardrail: Require material NIFTY exposure, not every small subsidy
LLM guidance: Government sector support: subsidy, PLI, procurement, allocation. New or expanded support for a sizeable sector = +1; withdrawal or cuts = -1. Only count actual policy actions, not proposals, wishlists or lobbying.

Event type: India sovereign rating or outlook change
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Country risk and financing conditions
Required guardrail: Obtain rating-agency release; geography follows India as subject

Event type: Foreign fiscal package or sovereign-risk shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Global bond yields and risk allocation
Required guardrail: Domestic and international fiscal effects need separate channels

Event type: NIFTY heavyweight earnings or guidance surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Index-weighted earnings expectations
Required guardrail: Use current point-in-time constituent weights and surprises
LLM guidance: Earnings or guidance of a NIFTY heavyweight (the company named in the headline). Beat on estimates or raised guidance = +1; miss or guidance cut = -1. If the text gives no comparison with expectations, judge cautiously: set surprise=unknown and confidence <= 0.5. Broker opinions on the stock are not events: is_commentary=true.

Event type: Major bank asset-quality, governance or funding event
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Financial-system confidence and index concentration
Required guardrail: A small isolated company event is not automatically a macro signal

Event type: Auto sales or broad bank business-update surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Consumption, credit and sector earnings
Required guardrail: Check exact issuer filing time; avoid using later intraday releases
LLM guidance: Sector-wide monthly business updates (auto sales across makers, bank credit and deposit growth for the system). A single small company's update is not sector-wide: relates=false. Growth above expectations or the previous period = +1, below = -1.

Event type: Large contract, capex, M&A or systemic corporate action
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Index earnings and sector investment
Required guardrail: Require index or sector-wide materiality
LLM guidance: Large contract, capex, M&A or corporate action by a NIFTY company or one that is systemic. Small deals (clearly under ~0.5% of the company's size, or an obviously small company) -> relates=false. Large value-accretive wins = +1; value-destroying or blocked deals = -1.

Event type: Foreign enforcement/legal action affecting Indian heavyweights
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Governance, funding and country risk
Required guardrail: Add official DOJ/SEC source; allegations are not findings of guilt

Event type: Global technology or outsourcing bellwether earnings
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Indian IT demand and global technology risk appetite
Required guardrail: Use issuer IR filings and distinguish earnings from broad AI speculation
LLM guidance: Earnings or guidance of a global technology or outsourcing bellwether (Nvidia, Accenture, hyperscalers) as a read-through for Indian IT. Beat and raise = +1; miss or guidance cut = -1. Scandals or product news without earnings impact: low intensity.

Event type: AI competition, cost or capability shock
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: IT business-model and global technology valuation reset
Required guardrail: Do not assume every product launch is economically material

Event type: AI capex, software-disruption or spending repricing
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Indian IT demand, margins and valuation
Required guardrail: Use source facts; avoid circular inference from a falling share price

Event type: Material India AI/digital policy or industry-wide development
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Domestic IT demand and regulatory cost
Required guardrail: Conference publicity alone is not a signal
LLM guidance: Material India AI/digital policy or industry-wide development. Supportive for IT demand = +1; compliance-heavy regulation that raises costs = -1; routine announcements = 0 with relates=false.

Event type: Monsoon, drought, flood or heatwave surprise
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Rural demand, food inflation, power and logistics
Required guardrail: Compare weather outcome with seasonal expectations
LLM guidance: A NEW monsoon development: an IMD forecast or revision, a fresh rainfall-deficit figure, a flood, drought declaration or heatwave event. A recap of a deficit or weak monsoon that is already known, with no new data, is not fresh: relates=false.

Event type: Public-health outbreak or restriction
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Mobility, consumption and activity risk
Required guardrail: Require official/reliable confirmation and avoid alarmist amplification

Event type: Global outbreak, disaster or critical supply-chain disruption
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Global demand or supply interruption
Required guardrail: Promote only events with an explicit India transmission channel

Event type: Crude oil price surge or slump
Seed aliases (expand semantically): Brent;WTI;crude price;oil price;barrel;crude jumps;oil tops;oil surges;crude slumps;oil prices fall
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Import bill, inflation, current-account deficit and rupee; oil-marketing and aviation margins (India imports most of its crude)
Required guardrail: Judge the size of the move and the level (e.g. a break above $100), not the mere mention of oil; a supply-shock rally is more bearish than a demand-led one; separate the price move from the war or supply event that caused it
LLM guidance: A surge in Brent/WTI (especially a break above $100 or a move of several percent in a day) is bearish; a slump is bullish. Judge the move reported in the text. Retail petrol and diesel pump prices are not crude price moves.
Exclude cues: petrol price today;diesel price today;petrol and diesel prices;pump price;olive oil;edible oil;cooking oil;coconut oil;oil painting

Event type: Foreign portfolio (FII/FPI) selling or buying in Indian markets
Seed aliases (expand semantically): FII;FPI;foreign investors;foreign portfolio investors;foreign institutional investors;net sellers;net buyers;foreign outflows;foreign inflows;FII selling
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Foreign investors are the marginal buyer of large caps: sustained selling pressures the index and the rupee, sustained buying supports both
Required guardrail: Use the stated net flow (Rs crore or dollars) and its direction versus recent days; one small day is minor, a multi-day streak or a record amount is major; domestic institutions' buying partly offsets
LLM guidance: Net selling by FIIs/FPIs is bearish and net buying is bullish. Scale the size by the amount and by streaks (longest selling streak, record outflow). Opinion about where FIIs might invest is not a flow event.

Event type: Rupee depreciation or appreciation (USD/INR, RBI intervention)
Seed aliases (expand semantically): rupee;INR;USD/INR;rupee slumps;rupee record low;rupee weakens;rupee strengthens;rupee falls;RBI intervention;dollar-rupee
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Imported inflation, foreign investors' dollar returns and external-account stress; a weak rupee often accompanies oil spikes and FII selling
Required guardrail: Judge the direction and size of the move versus the previous close (paise or percent) and record levels; RBI intervention that halts a slide is less bearish than the slide itself
LLM guidance: Rupee depreciation (slumps, falls, record low) is bearish and appreciation is bullish. RBI intervention to defend the rupee signals pressure: mildly bearish unless it clearly stabilises the currency.
Exclude cues: pakistani rupee;nepali rupee;nepalese rupee;sri lankan rupee;mauritius rupee;rupee symbol

Event type: Global equity selloff or rally and risk sentiment (Wall Street, Asia, VIX)
Seed aliases (expand semantically): Wall Street;Nasdaq;S&P 500;Dow Jones;Asian markets;global markets;global selloff;risk-off;risk appetite;VIX;stocks tumble;stocks rally
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Global risk appetite and emerging-market flows; overnight US and Asian moves set the opening gap
Required guardrail: Judge the move in major indices or in volatility as reported; a selloff concentrated in one sector or stock (e.g. AI stocks) is a narrower signal than a broad index fall
LLM guidance: A broad selloff in US or Asian equity indices, or a volatility spike, is bearish for NIFTY at the open; a broad rally is bullish. Stock-specific or sector-specific moves are small. Indian market wraps (Sensex, Nifty) are not global market moves.

Event type: US dollar and Treasury-yield spikes or drops (DXY, 10-year yield)
Seed aliases (expand semantically): dollar index;DXY;dollar surges;dollar jumps;10-year yield;Treasury yields;US yields;bond yields;yields hit multiyear highs
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: A stronger dollar and higher US yields pull capital from emerging markets, pressure the rupee and raise discount rates
Required guardrail: Judge the size of the move in the dollar index or the 10-year yield (basis points); separate a data-driven move (covered by the data seeds) from a pure rates repricing
LLM guidance: A sharp rise in the dollar index or in US yields (multi-year highs, jumps of 10 bps or more) is bearish; a sharp fall is bullish.
Exclude cues: dividend yield;yields over;high-yield savings;high yield savings;mortgage rates;cd rates;savings account

Event type: Heavyweight listing, IPO debut, demerger, large stake sale or buyback
Seed aliases (expand semantically): listing;IPO;market debut;shares list at a premium to the IPO price;strong debut;demerger;spin-off;stake sale;block deal;buyback;becomes most valuable company;market capitalisation jumps
NIFTY transmission hypothesis: Revaluation and liquidity effects on an index heavyweight: a listing or demerger that crystallises value lifts the parent and the index; large dilution or forced selling weighs
Required guardrail: Only a heavyweight (see the heavyweight list) or an event large enough to move the index counts; judge the move in the company's value (market cap, share price) the text reports, not the mere announcement
LLM guidance: A heavyweight's listing, demerger, stake sale or buyback that lifts its market value (e.g. Jio Platforms' debut lifting Reliance past rivals) is bullish; a large dilution, discount block deal or forced selling is bearish. Scale the size by the company's index weight. IPO chatter about small companies (grey-market premium, allotment status) is not an event.
Exclude cues: grey market premium;gmp today;allotment status;subscription status;sme ipo;ipo calendar
